title: Free-free and H42α emission from the dusty starburst within NGC 4945 as observed by ALMA
question: Measure free-free emission, electron temperature and star formation rate in the NGC 4945 central starburst from ALMA 85.69 GHz continuum and H42α, and compare with infrared and radio SFRs

what.value: Radio/mm flux densities 4.8-345 GHz used in SED fit

external_data.citation: healey07, lenc09, forbes98, roy10, massardi08, wang04, chou07, weiss08

what.value: Case B emissivities and recombination coefficients

recipe.method: clean cubes, continuum-subtract, sum channels 310-365 for H42α; median continuum over same channels
fit inclined thin exponential disc convolved with beam, and Gaussian
fit Gauss-Hermite functions (A, v0, sigma, h3, h4 free) to spectra and per pixel
fit power laws for synchrotron (free index), free-free (Gaunt factor, Te=5000 K), dust (index 4) to 3-350 GHz data
line-to-free-free continuum ratio with Storey & Hummer emissivities, case B, ne=1e3 cm-3

recipe.goal: SFR from ALMA, mid-IR, total IR, radio
recipe.method: Q from line/continuum; SFR=5.41e-54 Q; mid-IR via Rieke09; TIR via Murphy11; radio via Condon/Murphy
assumptions: Kroupa IMF, Z=0.040, continuous SFR >3 Myr

evidence.quote: 84%$\pm$10% of the 85.69 GHz continuum emission originates from free-free emission
The total continuum emission we measure with ALMA at 85.69 GHz is 0.36$\pm$0.02 Jy
The final SFR measured for the central source based on the total infrared flux is $3.0 \pm 0.3$ M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$.
we will work with a mid-infrared SFR measurement of 0.4 M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$
The mean barycentric velocity of 611$\pm$7 km s$^{-1}$

not_stated_but_needed: Region definitions for T, N, C, S apertures (only in figure)
Monte Carlo and Gauss-Hermite fitting algorithm details
Fit algorithm and optimizer for disc model
score_reason: Data public, recipe mostly specified with numeric results, but some imaging and fitting details missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public single-EB dataset, described imaging, numeric results (Te, SFR, scale length) can be checked.
